To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) NGS is a powerful diagnostic tool for PCD; 2) NGS is especially valuable for patients with normal or inconcusive ultrastructure and those without prior ultrastructure testing; 3) NGS is particularly useful for consanguineous patients, as it can identify the second pathogenic variant, even in the absence of parental testing, and can be used to identify the causative variant in patients with only one pathogenic allele
NGS is an accurate and rapid method for PCD diagnosis, which facilitates stratification according to ancestry, and can be used to identify families with a high risk of disease.

(i) NGS can identify the genetic cause of PCD in 82% of cases; (ii) NGS can facilitate PCD diagnosis in cases with normal or inconclusively normal ultrastructural results; and (iii) NGS reveals marked genetic stratification according the ancestry of PCD patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods to identify and characterise genetic variants in human populations.
the identification and characterisation of genetic variants in patients with primary ciliary dyskenesia (PCD) and the subsequent clinical utility of the genetic diagnosis in these patients.
the genetic and functional analysis of the primary ciliary dyskinetic (PCD) disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic testing of the PCD panel is highly useful in PCD diagnostics and can be applied to a wide range of patients.
NGS is a useful diagnostic test, especially in cases with normal or inconcusive ultrastructural analysis.
NGS has a significant added value in the diagnosis of PCD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that NGS can be used to diagnose PCD in 81% of cases with normal/inconclusive ultrastructure and in 67% of cases with no ultrastructure.
we have demonstrated that NGS is an efficient and effective diagnostic tool to diagnose a significant proportion of patients with PCD and has the potential to facilitate earlier diagnosis.
NGS is a valuable tool in the diagnosis and stratification of patients with PCD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetic stratification of PCD according to population of ancestry is a reality.
the genetics of PCD is highly heterogeneous.
